body: I'd like to get the invite for this and future WHATNOT meetings.
I added an Agenda+ to https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10233 as I have an early [PR](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11981) for it.
@janewman can you send me an email (cwilso at google) so I can add you?

I added Agenda+ to these items, both follow-ups from TPAC for working towards stage 2:

- [FormControlRange Interface · Issue #11478 · whatwg/html](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11478)  
- [[focusgroup] Declarative keyboard focus navigation for a scoped set of composite widgets · Issue #1…](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11641)

Attendees:
Olli Pettay, Chris Wilson, David Baron, Anne VK, Stephanie Zhang, Noam Rosenthal, Kurt Catti-Schmidt, Leo Lee, Kagami Rosylight, Jacques Newman, Luke Warlow, Joey Arhar, Brian Kardell, Vladimir Levin

Minutes:

- **Follow-up on Issue 11835 (Edge Cases)** Chris Wilson inquired about the status of issue 11835 concerning edge cases, which seemed to be waiting for notes from Emilio. Olli Pettay suggested that the hold-up might be waiting for feedback from other browser vendors. Chris Wilson agreed to remove the agenda plus label for now, and Olli Pettay offered to contact Emilio.
- **Updating Minutes for WHATSUP** Anne van Kesteren asked Chris Wilson if they still planned to add the minutes to the WhatsApp issue.  Chris confirmed they would address the task later today.
- **Out-of-Order HTML Streaming (Issue 11542)** Noam Rosenthal reported that they had completed a detailed write-up for issue 11542 regarding out-of-order HTML streaming, including a link to it. They noted that the proposal was simplified by removing `prepend` and `replace` methods, meaning the streaming can only replace all children or append, which fits the model of using a placeholder for an HTML stream. Noam Rosenthal also mentioned that if the target element is not found, the template is simply attached to the document and treated as a regular element, similar to a declarative shadow DOM on an element that cannot have one. Olli Pettay requested clarification on the definition of `append` in the explainer, stating that it appeared vague. Noam Rosenthal explained that `append` changes the insertion location from being inside the template to the real element; they mentioned that the Pull Request (PR) is very detailed, while Olli Pettay noted the explainer needs improvement. Anne van Kesteren questioned the need for `append` versus using ranges, but Noam Rosenthal argued that using ranges for multiple appends would become messy with numerous end-of-comment ranges. Noam Rosenthal agreed to add more examples to the explainer to clarify the use case for `append`, particularly when data comes asynchronously in the same HTML stream.  Anne van Kesteren raised the issue of consistency between out-of-order HTML streaming and the general streaming design questions for stream HTML. Noam Rosenthal indicated that they are currently treating them separately, as they found they share very little code or specification in common, except for a synergy where streaming append with JavaScript should apply template-based changes. Anne van Kesteren stressed the need to consider an asynchronous case for an async patch and for the API to remain consistent. Chris Wilson suggested removing issue 11542 from the agenda until they are ready to bring it back.
- **Support JSON and Style as Module Preload Destinations (Issue 10233)** Kurt Catti-Schmidt raised issue 10233, proposing support for JSON and style as module preload destinations, which was relevant to the declarative CSS modules discussion. They were following up on comments from Anne van Kesteren regarding whether JSON should be disallowed for a regular `link rel=preload`. Kurt Catti-Schmidt concluded that disallowing JSON for regular preload seemed reasonable and they would update the spec, add tests, and work on filling out the required checkboxes, noting this is a spec update that does not need stages.
- **Declarative Keyboard Focus Navigation/Scope Set of Composite Widgets (Issue 11641)** Jacques Newman sought to move the focus group proposal towards stage two, asking for feedback on whether the rough API shape in the spec is the right approach. Anne van Kesteren and Olli Pettay confirmed that reviewing the spec is the current action. Anne van Kesteren raised concerns about how the proposal interacts with existing platform conventions, such as Mac OS focus settings. Jacques Newman clarified that the feature only operates on keyboard-focusable elements and allows user agents to define what a natively focused element is, which they believed allows user agents to decide on restrictions. Anne van Kesteren mentioned that they need to consult with people more familiar with focus, and this review might take some time, though they aim to provide an estimate within two weeks. Someone in Monsters University (Hybrid Meeting Room) (us-cam-5cc) expressed support for the work, noting it addresses a problem web developers currently solve with a lot of JavaScript. Olli Pettay agreed on the idea's merit but emphasized that the key issue is how it integrates with the rest of the platform's focus handling. Luke suggested aligning the focus group with platform features that already have similar behavior, such as radio groups, to promote consistency and resolve subtle differences in edge cases currently handled by JavaScript. Jacques Newman requested confirmation that this review is blocking for stage two, which Anne van Kesteren confirmed.
- **Form Control Range Interface (Issue 11478)** Stephanie Zhang provided an update on the form control range discussion, now moving towards stage two, incorporating feedback received at TAC. Key changes include renaming the proposal (proposing "plain text range" but open to suggestions), no longer exposing internal nodes (making it fully value-space only), and making it more future-proof beyond just `input` and `textarea`. Olli Pettay noted that the explainer needs to be updated to reflect the substantial changes in the proposal. Anne van Kesteren questioned the name "plain text range" given that the agreement at TAC might have included support for arbitrary ranges with hidden start and end nodes. Stephanie Zhang explained that they chose "plain text range" for its alignment with value space and because it was less vague than suggestions like "element range". Leo Lee clarified that they are not married to the current name and are open to alternatives like "opaque range" or "shadow range". Leo Lee confirmed that the spec PR is up and linked, and the action item is for Stephanie Zhang to update the explainer and provide an update to the issue.
- **Improving Agenda Management and Review Visibility** Chris Wilson proposed creating a separate label for issues explicitly needing attention or review, distinct from the `Agenda Plus` label. Olli Pettay supported removing `Agenda Plus` by default for discussed items and requiring it to be added back for future discussion, noting that items posted close to the meeting time are difficult to review.  No action yet.
